A few leveling notes so we score consistently:
- "Senior (IC4)" expectations: delivers end-to-end designs that ship in a team; clearly weighs engineering tradeoffs; owns a component and mentors others.
- "Senior+" signal: sustained cross-team influence, carries design across multiple services, strong track record of production incident leadership and cost/latency wins.

Please use the matrix to mark: technical depth, tradeoff reasoning, execution plan, and behavior/partnering. I'll add a short candidate-specific prompt at the top of the matrix before we send to Alex.

Thanks Kim — I like the split. Couple of practical requests before I confirm calendars: 

1) Can we add one "canary" question for the panel that forces tradeoff articulation? Example: "You have a model serving pipeline with 3ms median token latency, but 1% of requests see 200ms spikes. Walk us through your triage and long-term mitigations." Ask interviewers to press for both immediate mitigations and long-term design changes.

2) For scoring: please weight tradeoff reasoning 30%, execution plan 25%, depth 25%, partnering/communication 20% — that distribution helps reduce variance across interviewers.

3) I'll take point on scheduling logistics; send me availability windows and I'll put tentative invites on the calendar (I'll use the calendar link in the shared Drive to keep everything consistent).

I attached a short debrief template too (we'll use in the same Drive folder) and will ping you if anyone needs an alternate slot.

Adding two quick notes from a leveling perspective (came up in a previous hiring sync):

- When scoring "depth" look for a clear problem decomposition (latency vs memory vs correctness) and at least one concrete experiment or benchmark the candidate would run. High depth candidates sketch at least one measurable experiment.

- For "impact" differentiate between owning a single service vs owning a cross-team runtime feature (cache semantics, KV API, or batching infra). If someone leads cross-team rollout for a runtime feature that reduces unit cost or latency cluster-wide, that's a strong Senior+ signal.

Also attaching a draft "leveling-descriptors-draft.docx" with short blurbs you can paste into the matrix. I recommend we read it quickly before debriefs to align thresholds.
